archetypes.name: floor-propagation
archetypes.rationale: The plan lowers Python 3.12→3.11 across 10+ files; verify every occurrence is updated and no dev-tooling-only 3.12 pin is accidentally lowered.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the plan's Python floor lowering (3.12→3.11) for completeness across every in-scope file: python/pyproject.toml, python/ruff.toml, python/pyrightconfig.json, python/.pylintrc, python/README.md, docs/installation-and-setup.md, skills/implement/SKILL.md, skills/report-tokens/scripts/run-analysis.sh, skills/report-tokens/scripts/test-run-analysis-quiet.sh, and .github/workflows/ci.yaml. Verify that the plan explicitly preserves dev/pre-commit tooling at 3.12 (docs/installation-and-setup.md line 297) and does not accidentally lower those pins. Check that the CI matrix change keeps pre-commit and topology setup-python steps pinned to 3.12 while running python-lint and python-tests under both 3.11 and 3.12. Flag any in-scope file whose plan entry still references 3.12 for runtime use, or any in-scope file the plan omits that contains a 3.12 runtime literal (e.g. within python/). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: acceptance-test-gap
archetypes.rationale: The issue lists explicit acceptance criteria; verify each maps to a named test with assertions strong enough to gate the criterion rather than just exercising the code path.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-check every acceptance criterion in the issue description against the named tests in the plan. For '#3 covered by real-CLI/recorded-fixture integration test', verify whether the test_gh.py additions actually include a real-CLI or recorded-fixture path or only stub-based assertions. For '#7 regression test pins a single CI cycle on a clean green path', verify the test_merge.py convergence test description is specific enough to gate the no-flush constraint and not merely assert flush was not called on a trivial mock. For 'Operational errors yield JSON result + routing exit code (never traceback/exit 1)', verify test_ship.py asserts the specific exit code 4 and that stdout contains valid JSON. For 'repo-wide git status --porcelain is empty after restore/clean', verify test_run_logs.py exercises the full restore+clean+status assertion rather than only checking the commit was skipped. Flag any acceptance criterion the plan addresses only via a weaker proxy assertion or leaves untested. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: stdout-contract
archetypes.rationale: Plan adds stderr breadcrumbs and remaps ShipError to STALLED; verify the JSON-only stdout and exit-code contract is airtight end-to-end between ship.py, ci_monitor.py, SKILL.md consumers, and the orchestrator routing layer.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that every plan change preserves the JSON-only stdout and exit-code contract at the ship.py driver boundary. Check that the new _breadcrumb helper writes exclusively to stderr and that no call site in ship.py or ci_monitor.py can accidentally write to stdout. Verify that the _error_to_result ShipError→STALLED branch maps to exit code 4 (EXIT_STALLED) consistently with OUTCOME_EXIT_MAP in config.py, and flag any risk that a concurrent sibling issue (#3446) editing OUTCOME_EXIT_MAP could silently override this mapping. Confirm that the plan's ci_monitor.py breadcrumb addition uses _warn_stderr (not print or sys.stdout) and leaves poll_ci's stdout path unchanged. Check whether the SKILL.md Step 8+ consumer parses ship.py stdout via a strict JSON parser that would break if a stderr breadcrumb were to contaminate stdout under any shell redirection pattern. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
